caea65bb7f902811d98ae257c767274fee58b95a.summary: Kaspersky GReAT report (published 2017-02-08) on fileless attacks against enterprise networks. After an incident response at a bank, it describes memory-resident Meterpreter and Mimikatz use, PowerShell scripts stored in the registry, and Windows SC and NETSH utilities used to install a service and build tunnels. Admin credentials were collected. Over 100 enterprise networks were found infected with related PowerShell scripts, but the report cannot confirm they share one attacker. The closest matching groups are Carbanak and GCMAN, and the report says attribution is almost impossible.

ca8958c804a7df2c8d79e14d5036648ec9eb6836.summary: PolySwarm blog post summarising Positive Technologies' report on the Space Pirates espionage campaign. The group targeted Russian aerospace, government and critical infrastructure, and also Georgia and Mongolia, with reported activity against Chinese financial entities. Activity is dated from late 2019 to mid-2021. The report presumes Chinese nexus but says the TTPs do not clearly match a known APT group. Tools include MyKLoadClient, Zupdax, RTLShare, PlugX and Deed RAT, with spearphishing as the initial access method.

ca9e79099adf463a4d9d31c0cc20515303bdd9c0.summary: Commentary by a Forescout Vedere Labs senior security researcher on the May leak of LockBit 4.0's affiliate panel, which exposed more than 4,000 chat messages, ransomware builds and cryptowallet data. The author argues that RaaS affiliates are opportunistic and disorganized: some ignored victims, delivered broken decryptors, attacked Russian government entities against platform rules, and most earned little from extortion. The author says this chaos makes the groups harder to defend against and expects more infighting, harder attribution, and preparation rather than negotiation as the main…

ca0cbfee8a829814d33da9fe4232515de86f4a9f.summary: US Department of Justice press release on the April 2021 sentencing of Fedir Hladyr, a high-level manager and systems administrator of FIN7 (also called Carbanak Group), to ten years in prison. Per the report, FIN7 ran a malware campaign since at least 2015 against hundreds of US companies, mainly in restaurant, gaming and hospitality, and stole more than 20 million card records. The report estimates overall damage at more than $3 billion. Hladyr was arrested in Germany in 2018 and pleaded guilty in September 2019.
